subject: maths
question: P sells an item to R at a profit of 10%, and R sells it to Q at a profit of 5%. What would have been P's profit percentage if he had sold the item directly to Q at the price R sold it?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let CP = 100

P → R at 10% ⇒ price = 110

R → Q at 5% ⇒ price = 110 × 1.05 = 115.5

Direct selling price = 115.5

Profit = 115.5 − 100 = 15.5%

**∴ Answer = 15.5%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

P sells to R at 10% profit, R sells to Q at 5% profit

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (1 + profit/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let cost price of P = 100

⇒ Selling price to R = 100 × 1.10 = 110

⇒ R sells to Q = 110 × 1.05 = 115.5

⇒ If P sold directly to Q, SP = 115.5

⇒ Profit = 115.5 − 100 = 15.5

⇒ Profit% = 15.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 15.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Profit

Overall multiplier = (1 + a/100)(1 + b/100)

Combined Profit

Net profit% = a + b + (ab/100)

Shortcut Insight

Use multiplication of factors instead of step-by-step calculation.
